papers.title: 3D bioprinting of stem cells and polymer/bioactive glass composite scaffolds for bone tissue engineering
papers.abstract: A major limitation of using synthetic scaffolds in tissue engineering applications is insufficient angiogenesis in scaffold interior. Bioactive borate glasses have been shown to promote angiogenesis. There is a need to investigate the biofabrication of polymer composites by incorporating borate glass to increase the angiogenic capacity of the fabricated scaffolds. In this study, we investigated the bioprinting of human adipose stem cells (ASCs) with a polycaprolactone (PCL)/bioactive borate glass composite. Borate glass at the concentration of 10 to 50 weight %, was added to a mixture of PCL and organic solvent to make an extrudable paste. ASCs suspended in Matrigel were ejected as droplets using a second syringe. Scaffolds measuring 10 × 10 × 1 mm3 in overall dimensions with pore sizes ranging from 100 – 300 µm were fabricated. Degradation of the scaffolds in cell culture medium showed a controlled release of bioactive glass for up to two weeks. The viability of ASCs printed on the scaffold was investigated during the same time period. This 3D bioprinting method shows a high potential to create a bioactive, highly angiogenic three-dimensional environment required for complex and dynamic interactions that govern the cell’s behavior in vivo.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文涉及骨组织工程的3D生物打印，但未包含任何人工智能或机器学习方法，与AI生物打印方向无关。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not incorporate AI/ML into any stage of bioprinting workflow, lacks autonomous decision-making or intelligent optimization.

summary_zh.motivation: 合成支架内部血管生成不足是骨组织工程的主要限制。
summary_zh.method: 将人脂肪干细胞与PCL/硼酸盐生物玻璃复合物共打印制备支架。
summary_zh.result: 支架降解可控释放生物玻璃，打印的ASCs在两周内保持存活。
summary_zh.validation: 通过体外细胞培养验证支架的降解性和细胞存活率。

summary_en.motivation: Insufficient angiogenesis within synthetic scaffolds limits bone tissue engineering. This study aims to enhance angiogenic capacity by incorporating borate glass into bioprinted scaffolds.
summary_en.method: Human adipose stem cells (ASCs) were bioprinted with a polycaprolactone (PCL)/bioactive borate glass composite using a dual-syringe system to create scaffolds with controlled porosity.
summary_en.result: Scaffolds exhibited controlled release of bioactive glass over two weeks, and printed ASCs maintained viability during the same period.
summary_en.validation: In vitro degradation and cell viability assays were conducted to validate scaffold performance.
